comment: Lore (issue #56), written by `packbuilder build` and `packbuilder lore-review`; read it in build/lore/<pack id>/review.md. Per species: the fact sheet the lore was written from (shipped with it), the sentences with the fact ids each rests on, the tagline, the model and prompt version, and the review: pending, approved (in the pack) or rejected (written again by the next build, with the reason).

facts.text: Its wingspan is estimated at about 26 cm from its wing length.
It feeds mostly on insects and other invertebrates.
It lives mostly in rocky places.
It stays in its range all year.
It spends most of its time perched in trees and shrubs.
It lays 1 to 6 eggs in a clutch.
The IUCN Red List rates it Least Concern.
The black phoebe is a passerine bird in the tyrant-flycatcher family.
The phoebes are a genus, Sayornis, of birds in the tyrant flycatcher family.
The black phoebe breeds in the west and southwest United States, Mexico and Central America, and parts of South America.
It has predominantly black plumage, with white on its belly and undertail coverts.
It breeds from southwest Oregon and California south through Central and South America.
The flycatchers are the largest family of birds on earth, with over 400 known species.
In Oregon it is found in river valleys on the Pacific coast, and in California on the western side of Coast Ranges.
The white forms an inverted "V" in the lower breast.

sentences.text: Hear now of the Black Phoebe, of the tyrant-flycatchers, the largest bird family on earth, over four hundred kinds strong.
Clad in black, it bears white upon its belly, where a pale V stands upside down on its lower breast.
It weighs about nineteen grams, yet its wings spread about twenty-six centimeters.
From tree and shrub it keeps watch over rocky places all year, feeding on insects and nesting in a cup.

tagline.text: The black-clad tyrant-flycatcher of the rocky places
